## Bug Analysis

**Root Cause:** In `TagsHelper.java`, the `removeTag` method (lines 87-93) uses `String.replaceAll()`:

```java
title = title.replaceAll(tagToRemove.getText(), "");
content = content.replaceAll(tagToRemove.getText(), "");
```

`replaceAll()` performs **substring** replacement. When removing `#test`, it also removes `#test` from within `#testa` and `#testb`, leaving only `a` and `b`.

**Fix:** Add a word boundary (`\b`) after the tag text so only complete tag matches are replaced.

## Summary

### Bug Diagnosis

**Location:** `TagsHelper.java`, method `removeTag()` (lines 88-94)

**Root Cause:** The `removeTag()` method used `String.replaceAll()` with a plain string pattern:
```java
title = title.replaceAll(tagToRemove.getText(), "");
```
This performs **substring** replacement. When removing `#test`, it also removes `#test` from within `#testa` and `#testb`, destroying those similar tags.

**Evidence:**
- Buggy: `"#test #testa #testb"` → `"a b"` (destroys similar tags)
- Fixed: `"#test #testa #testb"` → `"#testa #testb"` (only removes exact match)

### Fix Applied

**Two files modified:**

1. **`TagsHelper.java`** — Added word boundary matching:
   - Added `import java.util.regex.Pattern;`
   - Changed `replaceAll(tagToRemove.getText(), "")` to `replaceAll(Pattern.quote(tagToRemove.getText()) + "\\b", "")`
   - `Pattern.quote()` escapes any regex-special characters in the tag text
   - `\\b` ensures only complete word boundaries match, preventing partial matches

2. **`TagsHelperTest.java`** — Added test case `removesTagsFromNotePartialMatch()` that verifies removing `#test` doesn't affect `#testa` or `#testb`
